4. Mr. Azizur Rahman Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, has taken us through the first information report, depositions of the prosecution witnesses, the judgment of the learned Additional Sessions Judge and other relevant records of the Case. He has submitted that having regard to the evidence ofP.W.1 that he did not see the appellant calling his son JituMiah and that his daughter P.WA Ferdous Begum @ Rabea had been sleeping from before the time of calling of JituMiah by the appellant and NoushaMiah, P.W.I and 4 did not see the calling of JituMiah and having regard to the discrepancy in the evidence of r.ws. 2 and 4 namely, that P.W.2 stated that the accused appellant came up to the door of the hut of the informant P.W. 1 but P.WA stated that the appellant went inside the hut and sat there, P.Ws. 2 and 4 cannot be relied upon and therefore the order of conviction and sentence based on the evidence of P.Ws. 1, 2, and 4 as to calling of Jitu Miah by the appellant is not sustainable. He has further submitted that there are discrepancies in the evidence of P.Ws. 1,4,6,8,9 and 12 who have deposed about blood-stains and as such the order of conviction and sentence based on their evidence as to seeing blood stains is not sustainable. He has also submitted that some of the alleged blood-stained articles mentioned by some of the witnesses having not been seized by the Investigating Officer and Investigating. Officer having not sent the blood stained articles seized by him to the chemical examiner to ascertain if the blood in the seized articles was human blood so as to connect it with the murder of JituMiah although the Investigating Officer was required to send the blood-stained articles to the chemical examiner as the blood-stained articles were not seized from the place where the dead body was found, the prosecution has failed to connect the blood in the seized articles with the murder of deceased JituMiah. He has next submitted that non-examination of the neighborsAn sab Ali and Abdullah and others who were present in the house of the accused appellant in the morning following the night of occurrence and non-examination of the seizure list witnesses Abdul Sobhan, Md. BazlurRahman. andAnsabullah raises an adverse presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against he prosecution case. The last submission of the learned Advocate is that the deceased JituMiah was a man of bad character and cattle lifter and as such he had many enemies and he might have been killed by some of them elsewhere and not in the manner, at the time and place as alleged by the prosecution, 

 8. With regard to the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that non-examination of the neighbours Ansab, Abdullah and the seizure list witnesses AbdusSobhan, Md. Bazlur Rahman and Md. Asabullah raises a presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, we like to say that since we have already held that the prosecution has failed to prove the story of calling of Jitu by the appellant or Nausha and the seizure of blood-stained articles from the hut of appellant Siddik, we are not required to advert to this submission. In support of the sub-mission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the deceased Jitu had many enemies who might have killed him elsewhere in a manner other than what has been alleged by the prosecution, we find sufficient evidence on record to show that Jitu was a bad character and was involved in a number of cattle-lifting cases and he had many enemies. It is also in evidence that there was a warrant against him for which he was absconding. Therefore, the possibility of his being killed by some of his enemies elsewhere in a manner and at a time and place other than what has been alleged by the prosecution cannot be ruled out.
